# E27b-p99-engine — read latency tails under eviction, N against P+ and H3

*Generated by `cargo run --release -p comparator -- render --study e27b --shape p99-engine` from the point files in `results/E27b-p99-engine/`. Every number below is read from those files; none is typed. Cycle 15, round 2, card C15-02 (E27b part 1); pre-registered in `docs/study/E27b-design.md` (commit `77997dd`) before any engine change.*

**Why this file exists.** The engine rule's p99 clause is judged on q1 and q2 at 1 and 4 clients in this shape (design §4.2, §6), as E27 judged it in `results/E27-p99-engine.md`. N, P+ and H3, the rule's three arms; N as changed by E27b's E1–E4 and run as the metered build. The rule is evaluated in `results/E27b-comparator.md` §8, from this file's verdicts and the main sweep's memory verdicts.

### The arms

| arm | what it is |
|---|---|
| N | Nilestream daemon, metered build (`nilestreamd-metered`: the shipped `main.rs` compiled by `tools/memprobe` over a thread-local metering allocator, release) on 127.0.0.1:5450, --durable (SyncPolicy::Always), --mode demand, LRU, --checkpoint 16, budget 5% of keys; served relation (txn, acct, cur, amt, idem, value_date) |
| P+ | PostgreSQL 16, own cluster on 127.0.0.1:5452, SCRAM-SHA-256 as role bench: the E14 mechanism (partial slots, LRU, C = 16 checkpoints, anchored reconstruction) with the two cycle-14 repairs of sql/pplus.sql; append-only trigger |
| H3 | PostgreSQL 16 append-only ledger (own cluster on 127.0.0.1:5461, SCRAM-SHA-256 as role bench, append-only trigger) + `rev-sidecar` on 127.0.0.1:5462: logical replication (pgoutput, commit order as epoch order) into a nilestream-core REV, demand mode, LRU, budget 5% of keys, upquery `epoch <= e` on the ledger's index; q1 and q2 from the REV, q3–q6 relayed to PostgreSQL; a write is acknowledged once its epoch is in the view |

PostgreSQL configuration, identical on every PostgreSQL arm (§5.3), each non-default with its reason:

| setting | value | why |
|---|---|---|
| `shared_buffers` | `1GB` | cycle-13 Part 4, identical per arm |
| `synchronous_commit` | `on` | a commit is on stable storage when acknowledged, as on N |
| `fsync` | `on` | the same durability contract as N's SyncPolicy::Always |
| `wal_level` | `logical` | H3 reads logical replication; set on every arm so they stay alike |
| `max_connections` | `64` | room for 4 concurrent clients per arm with margin |
| `random_page_cost` | `1.1` | the data directory is on solid-state storage |
| `jit` | `off` | so plan-time variance is not attributed to an arm |
| `listen_addresses` | `'127.0.0.1'` | local only |
| `unix_socket_directories` | `'/var/run/postgresql' (root) or '/tmp' (elsewhere)` | where tools/pg-provision.sh's psql looks by default |

### Deviations from the specification, and repairs

- **Attempt 1 is disclosed and not pooled.** The first sweep (C15-02, 2026-10-01) stopped at single 10⁵, seed 1, on the refusal rule (design §9): N answered q3 — an ungrouped `count`/`sum` over one account, currency and value-day window with no postings in it — with no row, where SQL answers one row `(0, NULL)` (F-02-3). Its 20 points (10³ and 10⁴, both series, all five seeds) are kept in `results/E27b-comparator/attempt-1/`, classified historical in `results/MANIFEST.csv`, and none enters any figure in this file.
- **F-02-3 was fixed before this run** (C16-01, niles `3115d62`): an aggregate with an empty group key over an empty input answers one row — `count` 0, `sum`, `min`, `max` and `avg` NULL — on the reference evaluator and on every served path, and the grouped form still answers no row (`crates/niles-lang/tests/empty_scalar_aggregate.rs`, `crates/nilestream-server/tests/empty_scalar_aggregate.rs`). The change is in evaluation, not lowering: N's circuits did not move (the circuit-drift guard), and no other arm was touched. This sweep's driver stops on the first oracle divergence as well as the first failure; attempt 1's stopped only on failures.
- **q4 on N reads the desk from the account; no `desk` column was added** (design §2, E4, said N's served relation would gain one). The universe defines a desk as `acct % 16` (`universe::desk_of`), which is P's and M's spelling too, so a stored column would hold a function of a column N already has. N's q4 is `select cur, sum(amt) from postings where acct % 16 = {d} group by cur`, and its answers are held to the oracle like every other arm's. Decided in commit `44bb0cd`, before any run.
- **q3 on N writes its value-day window with `>=` and `<=`**: `between` does not lower on N's SQL surface. Design §5 provides for this ("the smallest spelling that does is used and listed as a deviation").
- **A four-value insert writes value date 0, not NULL** (design §2 said NULL): the ledger's valid-time field is an integer day, not an option. N's harness sends five values on every insert, so no measured read depends on it.
- **The E2 guard's third clause is false of the engine, so the guard records the behaviour instead of asserting the clause.** The clause is "stays bounded by the budget under eviction". Every evicted key leaves a `Hole` carrying its version (`crates/nilestream-core/src/absence.rs`). N's and H3's view-state bytes therefore grow by one hole per distinct key ever read, while their resident values and policy metadata stay at the budget (`tools/memprobe/tests/view_state_bytes.rs` asserts both halves). Whether a demand view keeps holes is LC-31, open since cycle 9. E27b measures the engine as it is. Found at the guard, before any E27b run.
- **N's view state counts three per-key maps besides the checkpoints** (`Ledger::checkpoint_state_image`). Two of them, the running balance and the posting count, place the checkpoints; P+ keeps the same as `arm.key_counts`, and its figure includes it. The third, `key_first`, is the first epoch per key, which E1's currency-named reads consult. It is closer to an index over the base, and it is counted anyway because counting it can only enlarge N's figure. P+'s figure adds `arm.rev_meta`, which E27's state table did not list.
- **The instrument, as built.** N runs as `nilestreamd-metered` and H3's sidecar as `rev-sidecar-metered`. Each is the shipped `main.rs` compiled by `tools/memprobe` over `alloc::Metered`, because §9.10 keeps `unsafe` out of the workspace. The allocator does one thread-local flag test per allocation. It counts only on the thread that asked for a figure, so neither contention nor another thread's allocations enter a figure. Its cost on latency is not measured separately and is borne by N and H3 alike. A figure is a clone's live bytes: exact for the B-trees and hash tables, and a lower bound by spare vector capacity. The PostgreSQL arms' `pg_total_relation_size` includes page slack and dead tuples. The asymmetry is stated beside every figure (§5).
- **H1, H2 and T are not re-run** (design §3): H1 and H2 do not enter the engine rule, and T informs the write floor only. E27's T figures stand, cited from `results/E27-comparator.md` and never pooled with these.
- **P+ is the E14 mechanism with two repairs** (`crates/comparator/sql/pplus.sql`; the E14 files are untouched). E14's `rev_read` served a resident slot for any anchor at or below its version, so a historical read after later postings returned the current value. That is a wrong answer, and it would have refused every q2 comparison. Its eviction also ordered victims by last *change*, not last use. Here a slot answers anchor e only if its last change is at or before e and the view has applied e, and eviction is LRU on a read tick, as on N. Unchanged from E27.
- **P+ answers q4, q5 and q6 by folding the base**: the E14 mechanism is keyed point reads and has no view for them; P and M answer them from the materialised view. N answers q3–q6 by folding its base (its view is keyed point balances).
- **H3's write is acknowledged only when its epoch has arrived through logical replication and been applied to the REV**, so H3's reads are exact at the head, like N's and P+'s, and its write latency includes the replication hop. Its upquery is `epoch <= e` on the ledger's index, with no checkpoints; its q3–q6 are relayed to its PostgreSQL. Unchanged from E27.
- **Latency is client-observed over the PostgreSQL wire, simple protocol, literal statement texts**, on every arm. PostgreSQL plans each statement; Nilestream compiles each (its plan cache is keyed by text, so literal keys miss it). Neither arm is given prepared statements.
- **P's write is two round trips** (`post_txn`, then `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW CONCURRENTLY`), because the refresh cannot run inside a function; its commit latency includes both, which is P's contract.
- **Anchors are drawn uniformly** between a key's first epoch and the head; reads draw only keys that exist at their anchor, as in E27.
- **Concurrency phases are read-only** (writes run only in the 1-client mixed phase), as in E27.
- **Allocations per read are not measured on the served binary** (design §11): the metered build counts bytes held on request, not allocations per operation; E18 measures those in-process.
- **The 10⁶ point is not in this file**: it is C15-04's (Host C). The container holds 2 cores and 8 GB.
- **The targeted p99 re-run ran nine days after the main sweep, on E27b's build, by the author's decision of 2026-10-10.** The main sweep's driver stopped at multi-currency 10⁵, as its rule requires, before this step. The author chose to run it on the engine the design named: the binaries were built afresh at `6ecded8` in a separate worktree (every point records that commit and a clean worktree), not at the later head where C16-03 had already compacted holes. The container had been replaced in between (kernel `6.18.44-fc-v114` against the main sweep's `fc-v50`; same 2 cores and 8 GB). Every comparison in the p99 file is within that run, interleaved as designed. Only §8 joins the two runs, reading memory from the main sweep and p99 from this one, as E27 also did. The memory cgroup killed nothing during it, and no arm diverged. Many of its cells, most of them at 10⁵, are REFUSED by the warm-up MAD rule (`results/E27b-p99-engine-detail.md` gives each reason). They are refusals, not directions.
- **The sweep was interrupted once by a container restart and resumed, not restarted** (2026-10-01, about 02:45Z), while `single-10000-7` was running. A point's file is written only when the point completes, so that point had written nothing and the six already written were intact. The driver was started again unchanged with `--skip-existing`; it skipped the six and re-ran `single-10000-7` from its start. No point was discarded or merged with a partial one.
- **At multi-currency 10⁵ the memory cgroup killed N five times, once per seed** (kernel log: `nilestreamd-metered`, anon-rss 3.10–3.29 GiB each; the event at seed 7 also killed one PostgreSQL backend). Five arms are co-resident during a point on a host of 8,031 MiB; design §3 expected that dropping H1, H2 and T would keep 10⁵ within it, and at multi-currency 10⁵ it did not. Seeds 1 and 100: N died in a warm-up run. Its later queries are recorded as errors (`failed to fill whole buffer`, `Broken pipe`), which the comparator counts as divergences, and the next run's connection was refused, which ends a point. These are transport errors after the process died, not wrong answers. Both points are kept as written, with FAILURES and no measured run. By the renderer's rule a failure anywhere at a size refuses that size's seed-replicated metrics, so **view-state bytes per key read at multi-currency 10⁵ are REFUSED for every pair**, and the engine rule's memory clause is not evaluated there.
- **At seeds 7, 42 and 2024 of multi-currency 10⁵ the kill came after the tenth measured run**, during the end-of-run checks, when the comparator reads every leg back from each arm. The comparator reads the end checksum and the arm's state only if it can connect, and records nothing when it cannot. So none of the three records a failure, all three lack N's end checksum and end state, and seed 7 also lacks P+'s. The same OOM event killed one PostgreSQL backend, the likeliest reason P+ did not answer; which cluster it belonged to was not recorded. Their measured runs are complete for every arm, and §1 shows those end checksums as *not read*. The silent skip is a harness defect recorded for the next card. It was not repaired during the sweep, because changing the harness would change what the remaining points measure. Nothing was re-run or tuned. The driver's stop rule (stop on a failure or a divergence) stopped the sweep after this step, so the p99-engine re-run did not start.

## 2. Verdicts per size range, and crossovers

Two exceptions to the per-seed gate, pre-registered (design §4.1): `view_state_bytes_per_key_read` — the engine rule's memory metric — and `pss_growth_bytes_per_key_read` (secondary) are judged **across seeds** on each seed's last measured run (joint gate over the five values; no warm-up floor, since a seed has one such value), because their per-run values trend with the keys read so far and are not replicates.

Each cell is the size verdict over the five seeds (rule in `crates/comparator/src/stats.rs`, fixed before the first measured run): an arm when at least three seeds give it and none gives the other; *no difference* when at least three are no difference or below floor; REFUSED when three or more seeds are refused; *mixed* otherwise. In brackets, the seed tally: arm-A wins / arm-B wins / no difference or below floor / refused. Every underlying cell is in `results/E27b-p99-engine-detail.md`.

## 6. Oracle divergences

**None.** Every read of every measured and warm-up run, on every arm, at every point, returned the oracle's answer.

## 7. The five anomalies (§5.7)

*Not part of this shape: the probe runs once, with the main sweep (`results/E27-comparator.md` §7).*

## 8. The engine rule, evaluated (H-E1)

The rule, unchanged (design §8): **N is justified as a product** iff it beats P+ **and** H3 by the joint gate, above the floor, on view-state bytes per key read **and** on p99 read latency under eviction. **The hybrid** (PostgreSQL ledger + REV sidecar) is recommended iff H3 matches N within the gate on both; **PostgreSQL with the E14 mechanism** iff P+ matches N on both. *Matches* is read as the size verdict *no difference*. The p99 clause is q1 and q2 at 1 and 4 clients from the targeted re-run (`results/E27b-p99-engine.md`); a query NOT RUN there (q2 on `multi` at 10⁵, §6) is left out of the clause and said so. A recommendation that holds at one end of the sweep and not the other is two recommendations (S-1).

| series | pair | metric | source | 10³ | 10⁴ | 10⁵ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| multi | N vs P+ | q1_p99_us | p99 re-run | **N better** | no difference | mixed |
| multi | N vs P+ | q2_p99_us | p99 re-run | **P+ better** | **P+ better** | NOT RUN |
| multi | N vs P+ | c4_q1_p99_us | p99 re-run | no difference | no difference | **P+ better** |
| multi | N vs P+ | c4_q2_p99_us | p99 re-run | **P+ better** | **P+ better** | NOT RUN |
| multi | N vs H3 | q1_p99_us | p99 re-run | no difference | no difference | REFUSED |
| multi | N vs H3 | q2_p99_us | p99 re-run | **H3 better** | **H3 better** | NOT RUN |
| multi | N vs H3 | c4_q1_p99_us | p99 re-run | REFUSED | **H3 better** | REFUSED |
| multi | N vs H3 | c4_q2_p99_us | p99 re-run | **H3 better** | REFUSED | NOT RUN |
| single | N vs P+ | q1_p99_us | p99 re-run | **N better** | **N better** | no difference |
| single | N vs P+ | q2_p99_us | p99 re-run | **N better** | no difference | REFUSED |
| single | N vs P+ | c4_q1_p99_us | p99 re-run | REFUSED | REFUSED | REFUSED |
| single | N vs P+ | c4_q2_p99_us | p99 re-run | **N better** | **N better** | REFUSED |
| single | N vs H3 | q1_p99_us | p99 re-run | **N better** | **N better** | REFUSED |
